subject: Interim update: API availability impact — interim summary & next steps
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: kevin.liu@stellarapps.com, ops@stellarapps.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent API availability — interim summary & next steps

Hi Kevin / StellarApps ops team,

Quick status: we observed an elevated number of partial responses and 503s affecting a subset of hosted generation requests between ~08:35–09:40 PDT this morning. We opened an incident and have a temporary routing fallback active to reduce customer impact while we continue remediation.

What we know so far:
- Impact: ~1.8% of generation requests for model: redwood/text-gen-v3, primarily p95/p99 latency spikes and intermittent 503s.
- Root symptom (interim): a regressed prefix cache eviction path causing KV cache thrash on a subset of GPUs under certain sequence-length distributions.
- Mitigation in place: we enabled conservative cache TTLs and routed traffic away from affected GPU pool (fallback to a compatible variant) at 08:55 PDT.

Customer-facing actions we took:
- Status page entry published: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/rlg-2027-08-02
- Temporarily routed affected traffic to variant: text-gen-v3-stable (slightly higher cost, lower latency variability).

Next steps (today):
1) Complete short timeline and send an interim customer email with attached timeline and recommended client-side retries.
2) Run a targeted validation job against the fix branch and if green, schedule a controlled rollback of the cache change.
3) Provide a postmortem within 48 hours and coordinate follow-ups for any SLA/credit requests.

If you can share any additional logs (request IDs, example payloads) from StellarApps for the times above that would be helpful in correlation.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts production flows. We will follow up with a post-incident summary and concrete mitigation steps.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182

Attachment: incident_timeline_2027-08-02.pdf (timeline, interim mitigation notes)

Subject: Re: Intermittent API availability — interim summary & next steps

Hi Kevin — thanks for the request IDs. We've correlated s-app-req-7723/7728 and confirmed they hit the eviction window. Couple of clarifications and guidance for your team: 

Short-term guidance for clients:
- Use exponential backoff (start at 250ms, cap at 2s) with jitter for retries on 5xx.
- Reduce large-batch burst sizes where possible (we saw larger sequence-length batches amplify the eviction).

Expected fallback timeline:
- We plan to keep the fallback (text-gen-v3-stable) active through the validation run and controlled rollback window. Estimated 6–12 hours, contingent on test results. We will update the status page if that changes.

We are attaching an internal diff for the TTL revert (temporary-mitigation-config.diff) and a short timeline PDF. Once the rollback is validated in our canary pool we will lift the fallback and monitor for recurrence.

If StellarApps would like a short maintenance window to coordinate traffic shifts, we can schedule one this afternoon.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: temporary-mitigation-config.diff (config diff; checksum: sha256:abc123)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: kevin.liu@stellarapps.com, ops@stellarapps.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident: brief summary and next steps (railgate incident)

Hi Kevin — follow-up with the post-incident interim summary and commitments. Thanks for the patience.

Summary (what happened):
- Between 08:35–09:40 PDT on 2027-08-02, a recent config change reduced the effective prefix cache TTLs under certain sequence-length distributions. This caused repeated KV cache evictions on an affected GPU pool, leading to increased tail latency and a small percentage of 503s.

Impact:
- Customer visible: ~1.8% of generation requests across hosted API for text-gen-v3 (p95/p99 spikes), with StellarApps reporting visible errors in their ingestion pipelines.
- Duration of visible impact: ~1h 5m (before fallback routing)

Mitigation and recovery:
- 08:55 PDT: activated routing fallback to text-gen-v3-stable to reduce variability (mitigated user-visible errors).
- 10:20 PDT: validated rollback in canary; began staged rollout to affected pools.
- 12:05 PDT: fully reverted the TTL change; monitoring showed normal tail behavior resumed and no recurrence.

Actions taken / next steps:
1) Root cause fix: revert and additional safety guard around TTL changes (already applied).
2) Deployment process: add an additional canary gate for cache TTL modifications and a monitoring alert targeted at KV eviction rate.
3) Customer follow-up: we will publish a full RCA within 48 hours and make ourselves available for a joint review with StellarApps engineering.
4) SLA/credits: if StellarApps requests an SLA credit, we will follow standard review process — Laura will send details on documentation required to initiate claims.

Attached: incident_timeline_2027-08-02.pdf (concise timeline and signal excerpts), temporary-mitigation-config.diff

Again, apologies for the disruption. We prioritized a safe rollback and restored normal service within the day. If you'd like a short post-incident review call, propose a few times and we will accommodate.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
